pages.heading: Remote work & expenses
pages.text: This is a fictional operational handbook created for the Folio assignment. Effective 1 January 2025. The remote-work policy permits eligible employees to work remotely three days per week. Customer support staff must have at least two team members onsite each business day. New employees must work onsite for their first 30 calendar days before becoming eligible for remote work. Remote-work approval belongs to the employee's line manager. The 2024 allowance was two remote days per week. Employees receive a one-time home-office equipment allowance of INR 18,000 in 2025; the allowance was INR 12,000 in 2024. Claims require itemized receipts and manager approval. Claims must be submitted within 30 days of purchase. The handbook does not specify maternity leave entitlement or individual employee salaries.

pages.heading: Access & retention
pages.text: Production access requires manager approval and a hardware-backed multi-factor authentication factor. Access reviews occur every 90 days. When an employee leaves, production access must be revoked within four hours of the recorded departure. Customer support tickets are retained for 24 months after closure. Application logs are retained for 90 days, except security incident logs, which are retained for 365 days. A legal hold suspends scheduled deletion until the legal team releases the hold. The security team owns the legal-hold exception. Archived backups are encrypted at rest. The operations handbook does not define company revenue or product pricing.

pages.heading: Supplier onboarding
pages.text: New suppliers must complete a security questionnaire before receiving access to customer data. The procurement team owns the supplier register. Suppliers handling customer data must complete a security review every 12 months. Critical suppliers are reviewed every six months instead. A supplier is critical if its outage can stop production service for more than one hour. Supplier invoices are payable within 45 days of approval. Escalations about overdue invoices go to the finance operations team. The onboarding checklist requires a signed data processing agreement for every supplier processing personal data.

pages.heading: Severity & communication
pages.text: This fictional policy was effective from 1 January through 31 December 2024. A Severity 1 incident is a complete production outage or confirmed customer-data exposure. The on-call engineer must acknowledge Severity 1 incidents within 15 minutes. The incident commander must publish customer status updates every 60 minutes during a Severity 1 incident. Severity 2 incidents are partial service degradations without confirmed data exposure and require acknowledgment within 60 minutes. The incident commander coordinates response. The communications lead drafts customer notices.

pages.heading: Recovery objectives & review
pages.text: For the 2024 incident policy, the production recovery time objective (RTO) is four hours. The production recovery point objective (RPO) is 60 minutes. Encrypted database backups are taken every 60 minutes. A restore drill must be completed once per quarter. Every Severity 1 incident requires a blameless post-incident review within five business days of resolution. The review must identify the timeline, customer impact, contributing factors, and accountable remediation owners. The security team retains incident logs for 365 days. This policy does not describe 2025 recovery targets.

pages.heading: Severity & communication
pages.text: This fictional policy is effective from 1 January 2025 and supersedes the 2024 incident policy for incidents occurring in 2025. A Severity 1 incident is a complete production outage or confirmed customer-data exposure. The on-call engineer must acknowledge Severity 1 incidents within five minutes. The incident commander publishes customer status updates every 30 minutes during a Severity 1 incident. Severity 2 incidents require acknowledgment within 30 minutes. The security lead must join any incident involving suspected customer-data exposure. A status update must explicitly distinguish confirmed impact from impact still under investigation.

pages.heading: Recovery objectives & review
pages.text: For the 2025 incident policy, the production recovery time objective (RTO) is one hour. The production recovery point objective (RPO) is 15 minutes. Encrypted database backups are taken every 15 minutes. A restore drill is required every month. Compared with the 2024 policy, the RTO decreases from four hours to one hour and the RPO decreases from 60 minutes to 15 minutes. A blameless post-incident review is required within three business days of resolution of a Severity 1 incident. Remediation owners must record target completion dates. Security incident logs are retained for 365 days unless a legal hold applies. This policy does not specify the organization's insurance provider or annual revenue.
